prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger economy, fairer society: opportunity for everyone. The Liberal Democrats’ 2015 plan builds on delivery in government to finish balancing the books fairly, protect essential services, green the economy, and widen freedom and opportunity in an open, outward‑looking UK.

Responsible finances and fair taxes
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18 with a fair mix of spending restraint and targeted tax measures on wealth, big banks and polluters; debt to fall each year thereafter (outside recessions).
- No rises in Income Tax, National Insurance, VAT or Corporation Tax rates; raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500 (around £400 extra tax cut).
- Tough action on avoidance/evasion; reform reliefs; a High Value Property Levy on homes over £2m.

Prosperity for all: a high‑skill, low‑carbon economy
- Double economy‑wide innovation spend; expand Catapults; ringfence science and grow it in real terms.
- Expand the British Business Bank; promote competition and community/alternative finance.
- Devolve economic powers; 10‑year capital plans; HS2 as part of a national rail upgrade and mass electrification; complete East‑West Rail; Transport for the North.
- Green leadership: Zero Carbon Britain by 2050; power‑sector decarbonisation to 50–100g CO2/kWh by 2030 with around 60% renewables; end unabated coal by 2025; scale carbon capture, storage and smart grids; expand the Green Investment Bank with borrowing powers.

Real help for families: work, welfare and pensions
- 20 hours’ free childcare for 2–4 year‑olds and, for working parents, from end of paid leave; complete Tax‑Free Childcare; 85% childcare support in Universal Credit.
- Complete Universal Credit so work always pays; fair, time‑limited 1% cap on working‑age benefits until balance in 2017/18, protecting disability/parental benefits.
- Living Wage in central government; stronger rights on flexible work and shared parental leave; tackle gender pay gap.
- Make the State Pension ‘triple lock’ permanent; continue auto‑enrolment; protect pension freedoms.

An opportunity society: education and skills
- Protect education funding from nursery to 19; retain and strengthen the Pupil Premium; national fair funding formula.
- Qualified teachers in every class; Royal College of Teachers; evidence‑led slim core curriculum including PSHE and financial/life skills.
- Eradicate child illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025; double businesses hiring apprentices; expand high‑level apprenticeships; fair, access‑focused universities.

A healthier society: equal care for mental health
- At least £8bn extra a year for the NHS in England by 2020; integrate health and social care budgets locally by 2018.
- Mental health parity with £500m more by 2016/17; national waiting‑time standards; crisis care in every A&E; carers’ support and a £250 annual Carer’s Bonus.

Homes, communities and the environment
- Build 300,000 homes a year including at least 10 new Garden Cities; Rent to Own and Help to Rent; longer, more secure tenancies; tackle rogue landlords.
- Five Green Laws: Nature, Zero Carbon Britain, Green Transport, Resource Efficiency/Zero Waste (70% recycling target), and Green Buildings (Band C homes, council tax incentive).
- Clean air plan with Low Emission Zones; ULEV‑only cars by 2040; complete high‑speed broadband to 99.9%.

Freedom, democracy and security
- Protect the Human Rights Act; a new Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act; defend free speech.
- Votes at 16; STV for elections; replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill of Rights; evidence‑led drug harm reduction (Portugal model).
- Cooperative, proportionate security; step down the nuclear ladder while maintaining credible defence.

Britain in the world
- Lead in a reformed EU; complete the Single Market; support fair, protective trade deals; retain 0.7% aid; global climate leadership and human rights promotion.
</text>
